title: Bitcoin realized-volatility compression below QQQ
operational_status: Historical backtest running; prospective shadow initialized

source.image_description: TradingView chart comparing BTC and QQQ 30-day realized volatility, with historical BTC buy markers near periods when BTC realized volatility fell to or below QQQ realized volatility.
source_limitations: The repository record is grounded in the supplied chart image and URL; the full tweet text is not independently archived here.
Chart annotations are source evidence, not validation.
The source image does not expose machine-readable marker dates or indicator code, so exact marker reproduction is not claimed.

canonical_hypothesis: When Bitcoin 30-day realized volatility crosses below QQQ 30-day realized volatility, Bitcoin enters an unusually compressed volatility regime relative to large-cap US technology equities and subsequently earns stronger forward risk-adjusted returns than an unconditional Bitcoin holding benchmark.

canonical_trigger.btc_series: BTC daily close-to-close log-return realized volatility
canonical_trigger.qqq_series: QQQ daily close-to-close log-return realized volatility
canonical_trigger.annualization: sqrt(365) for BTC and sqrt(252) for QQQ
canonical_trigger.alignment_rule: Compare both metrics only on QQQ trading dates using information available after the QQQ close; use the latest completed BTC daily close available at that decision timestamp.
canonical_trigger.entry_event: First date on which BTC realized volatility is strictly below QQQ realized volatility after being greater than or equal to it on the prior comparable date.
canonical_trigger.anti_churn_rule: A new event cannot be registered until BTC realized volatility has first returned to greater than or equal to QQQ realized volatility.

execution_definition.entry: First completed BTC UTC daily close strictly after the QQQ-close decision timestamp
execution_definition.funding: Not applicable to the spot proxy

candidate_exit_tests: Exit on the first comparable date when BTC realized volatility returns to greater than or equal to QQQ realized volatility
primary_instrument: BTC spot total return before and after explicit execution costs
benchmarks: Unconditional BTC forward return at every eligible QQQ trading-date observation
Buy-and-hold BTC over the same sample
invalid_or_failure_regimes: single-stock or event-driven QQQ volatility spike that creates a denominator artifact
fewer than 10 independent historical trigger events
results driven by one market cycle
failure after realistic fees and slippage
trigger definition changed after observing outcomes

primary_success_target.metric: mean after-cost return improvement relative to the absolute mean of the calendar-year-matched unconditional benchmark

research_questions: Does the crossover improve BTC forward returns at 30, 90, 180 and 365 days?
Does it improve risk-adjusted performance or only select periods with high unconditional BTC drift?
How often does the trigger precede a further drawdown of 20% or more?
Is the effect stable across the predeclared price regimes?

initial_confidence.label: Preliminary
basis: The claim is mechanical and reproducible.
The supplied chart displays multiple historical examples.
The canonical definition and prospective boundary were frozen before the repository backtest result was reviewed.

next_stage_gate.target_stage: Backtest resolution and prospective watchlist decision
requirements: Store the auditable result and raw payload hashes.
Report the predeclared 90-day improvement target without changing the rule.
Update confidence using sample size, source-exposed validation, regime stability, costs and decay risk.
Keep production blocked until untouched prospective evidence exists.

governance_note: Canonical before enhanced. Historical evidence can grant watchlist status only; it cannot grant capital rights.
